2. TI compiler minor version is wrong in the C file — ceu_check_c_compiler.c:82 computes the minor as (ti_version / 1000000L) % 1000L, which just repeats the major. The C++ file (ceu_check_cxx_compiler.cc:49) has the correct (ti_version % 1000000L) / 1000. For TI 20.12.4 the C path prints "20.20.4".
3. Borland detection can break the build — ceu_check/cc/01_turboc.h maps __TURBOC__ with exact == comparisons and has gaps (e.g. 0x0580, 0x0571–0x058F) with no #else fallback, leaving CEU_CPPB_VERSION undefined; I reproduced the resulting compile error at ceu_check_c_compiler.c:314. Additionally, both compiler-info functions do arithmetic on __BORLANDC__ directly (ceu_check_c_compiler.c:311, ceu_check_cxx_compiler.cc:142), but detection can trigger from __TURBOC__/__BCPLUSPLUS__ alone, in which case __BORLANDC__ is an undeclared identifier — another compile failure.
4. -static-libgcc is silently never applied — CMakeLists.txt:26-27 uses $<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C> / $<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX> inside target_link_options, where that genex doesn't do what's intended. I checked your existing opt/1 link line: it contains -static -static-libstdc++ but no -static-libgcc. $<LINK_LANGUAGE:...> (CMake ≥ 3.18) is what belongs there.
5. Big-endian TI targets are classified little-endian — in ceu_check_arch_macros.h, the little-endian chain contains /* TIARMCLANG */ (defined(CEU_COMPILER_IS_TI) && !defined(__ARM_BIG_ENDIAN))). That clause matches any TI compiler that isn't ARM-Clang — including big-endian C6000/ARMCL builds, which define __big_endian__/__BIG_ENDIAN__ but never __ARM_BIG_ENDIAN. Since the LE chain is evaluated first, those targets get CEU_COMPILE_TIME_IS_LITTLE_ENDIAN. The clause needs a __clang__ qualifier.

Detection inconsistencies

6. GetVersionEx lies without a manifest (ceu_check_os.cc:141) — on Windows ≥ 8.1 it reports 6.2 unless the executable carries a compatibility manifest, so the entire Windows 10/11 build-number table below it is effectively unreachable in practice. RtlGetVersion (or a manifest) is needed for that table to ever fire. Related nits in the same table: the range 19042 <= build < 19044 for 21H1 overlaps the 20H2 range above it (works only by branch order), and the final else "Windows 10/11 unknown" is unreachable.
7. lsb-release probe contradicts its own comment — ceu_check_os.cc:242 says "Should be in /etc/os-release or /usr/lib/os-release" but the code reads /etc/lsb-release / /usr/lib/lsb-release. Modern distros ship os-release; on most systems this just prints "not found".
8. MSVC table issues (ceu_check/cc/08_msvc.h) — the clang branch hardcodes the string "Microsoft Visual Studio Clang Compiler" instead of using CEU_COMPILER_NAME_MSVC_CLANG (that constant in ceu_compiler_names.h is defined but never used anywhere); _MSC_VER == 900 is labeled VS "3" but 900 was Visual C++ 2.0 (there was no 3.0); and the > 1940 && < 1950 catch-all says "unknown later than 17.10" even though explicit branches up to 17.14 exist above it.
9. CEU_ON_MINGW32 doesn't mean 32-bit — ceu_check/os/03_windows.h sets it whenever __MINGW32__ is defined, which is also true on 64-bit MinGW-w64 (and via __WINNT__, which isn't a MinGW indicator at all). Both CEU_ON_MINGW32 and CEU_ON_MINGW64 end up defined on a 64-bit build.
10. Comment/label glitches: sparcv9 entries in the 64-bit chain of ceu_check_arch_macros.h are annotated /* Known 32-bit */; check_exe_main.cc labels the runtime bitness fallback "(Compile-time Sizeof)" and its "Unknown (Run-time)" endianness branch is unreachable (little is defined as !big); both Borland printers emit __CODEGEARC_VERSION__==UNDEFINED (double =), and the C++ one is missing a space before "compatible version number"; c_snprintf.h:7 says "Enable MSVC secure CRT functions" when _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS actually silences the insecure-function warnings.

Security-relevant observations

None of these are exploitable in a meaningful way for an info-dump library, but worth knowing:

- TOCTOU (CWE-367) at ceu_check_os.cc:249-256: access() then ifstream open. Harmless here, but the access() probe adds nothing — just try opening each file.
- Unchecked uname() return at ceu_check_os.cc:123; the struct is zero-initialized so it's not UB, but a failure silently prints empty fields.
- Verbatim output of external data: uname fields and lsb-release contents go raw to stdout, so a hostile (root-writable) file or hostname could smuggle ANSI escape sequences into a terminal. Low risk, but sanitizing control characters would close it.
- Build-metadata leakage: __DATE__/__TIME__ are embedded unless CEU_REPRODUCIBLE_BUILDS=1, yet that flag is consumed by libceu_stddef.h.in without ever being declared as an option() in CMakeLists — it only works if someone happens to know the cache variable name.
- Subproject hygiene (this repo lives in art_modern/deps/): configure_file writes libceu_stddef.h into the parent's ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/include rather than CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR, install(TARGETS slim_libceu) runs unconditionally and pollutes the parent's install, and file(GLOB) lacks CONFIGURE_DEPENDS.
